answer: Divergent-history proof-of-life. Each agent wanders through a public sequence of tasks whose correct answers depend on prior random inputs, so every identity's path is unique. Clones cannot vine off without later contradicting an earlier answer, and a shared path collapses to one identity at the sybil nadir. Enforcing one vote per distinct path costs an attacker a fresh independent run per identity, multiplying compute and time linearly.
